cards.narrative: Minnesota sues Greg Abbott to force extradition of an ICE agent accused of shooting a Venezuelan man.
cards.paragraph: Minnesota is taking Texas to court over an ICE agent who shot a Venezuelan man. The agent is accused in the shooting, and Minnesota wants him extradited. Governor Greg Abbott is refusing, so now it's a legal fight between two states.

cards.narrative: The hemp industry files a new lawsuit over Texas' THC ban claiming job losses and a medical marijuana monopoly.
cards.paragraph: Texas banned THC, and now the hemp industry is fighting back in court. They say the ban is costing jobs and handing a monopoly to medical marijuana companies. It's a legal battle over who gets to sell cannabis products in the state.

cards.narrative: A fan threw a green dildo onto the court during a WNBA game and got arrested and banned.
cards.paragraph: A green dildo landed on the hardwood during the Dream-Sparks game. The fan was arrested and banned. It's a recurring problem the league thought it had solved, but apparently not.

cards.narrative: The New York Times lost a $9.25 million defamation verdict to a former Alabama basketball player.
cards.paragraph: Kai Spears, a former Alabama basketball player, won a $9.25 million verdict against the New York Times. The paper falsely identified him as a passenger in a car at the site of a fatal shooting. The jury decided that mistake was worth millions.
cards.data_point: Former Alabama basketball player Kai Spears has been awarded $9.25 million by a Tuscaloosa jury after he sued the New York Times for defamation for falsely identifying him as a passenger in a car at the site of a fatal shooting.

cards.narrative: Marina Mabrey tied the WNBA single-game scoring record with 53 points in Toronto.
cards.paragraph: Marina Mabrey scored 53 points in a game, tying the WNBA record. She's become Toronto's newest star, and the front office rewarded her with a two-year, $2.4 million contract. That's a big deal for an expansion team.
cards.data_point: General Manager Monica Wright Rogers and the rest of the front office were happy to commit to Mabrey in the form of a two-year, $2.4 million contract.

cards.narrative: Matt Campbell's truth bomb about Penn State's expectations will catch fans' attention.
cards.paragraph: Matt Campbell, Penn State's new coach, described seeing Beaver Stadium's lights on during its expansion. He understands the expectations waiting for him. It's a glimpse into the pressure cooker of coaching a blue-blood program.

cards.narrative: Pierre 'P' Thomas, CEO of Quality Control, was hospitalized following a medical emergency.
cards.paragraph: Quality Control's CEO Pierre 'P' Thomas is hospitalized after a medical emergency. The company says he's alive and receiving care. He co-founded the label that brought us Migos, and in 2023 HYBE bought it for $300 million.
cards.data_point: In 2023, South Korean music company HYBE acquired Thomas and Lee's Atlanta-based powerhouse label (QC Media Holdings) for $300 million ($250 million in cash and $50 million in stock).

cards.narrative: Bezos' aerospace company Blue Origin could land a massive manufacturing plant in Hutto, Texas.
cards.paragraph: Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin is eyeing Hutto, Texas, for a manufacturing plant the size of 26 football fields. The $650 million project would join a host of Central Texas spaceflight companies. It's a big win for the small town's economy.
cards.data_point: The proposed Project Blue Hub plant will be about the size of 26 football fields – 1.3 million square feet at a cost of $650 million.

cards.narrative: Vantage Communities secured a $103 million refinancing for a three-property apartment portfolio in Austin and San Antonio.
cards.paragraph: Vantage Communities refinanced three apartment properties in Austin and San Antonio for $103 million. Benefit Street Partners provided the financing. It's a sign of continued investor confidence in Texas multifamily real estate.
cards.data_point: Vantage Communities has obtained a $103 million refinancing for a three-property, 864-unit multifamily portfolio located in the Austin and San Antonio metro areas.

cards.narrative: Cousins Properties sold the One Eleven Congress office tower in downtown Austin for $208 million.
cards.paragraph: Cousins Properties sold One Eleven Congress, a prominent Austin office tower, for $208 million. Canyon Creek Real Estate bought it. The sale shows the downtown Austin office market is still active despite remote work trends.
cards.data_point: Cousins sold the One Eleven Congress office building for $208 million.
